text:
elena: Drafting a lightweight PRD addendum for SLO acceptance + tiered throttling playbook. Main idea: avoid blunt rollbacks by doing progressive degradation (throttle, reduce model size, disable non-essential features) driven by error-budget burn and latency tiers. please review the acceptance criteria and edge-case checklist. link: https://redwood-internal/docs/prd/prudence-playbook

kevin: skimming — sounds reasonable. quick q: do we want token-based rate-limits or qps? token-based maps to cost better but implementation touches gateway + billing. for canary plan i suggest 10% traffic for 24h then 50% for 2h.

maya: +1 to progressive. from SRE POV we need clear burn-rate triggers and cooldown windows. propose: burn_rate > 2 for 15m => start soft-throttle (reduce concurrency by 20%), burn_rate > 5 for 5m => escalate to model-fallback and page oncall. alerting rules sketch:
```
ALERT ErrorBudgetHigh
IF burn_rate(metric_error_budget) > 2 FOR 15m
LABELS {severity="warning"}
```
and page when burn_rate > 5 for 5m.

jamal: model fallback risks: switching from baseline-13B -> low-lat-7B quantized will reduce latency but may change semantics. need a small eval set to gate quality drop (BLEU-ish / embedding-sim) before automatic fallback. also KV cache reuse will help — recommend reusing prefix cache across similar sessions when throttling.

sarah: important: enterprise contracts. some customers have strict SLA clauses that forbid model substitution without consent. propose: per-customer "fallback policy" flag: "allow-automatic-fallback" (default false for enterprise). If false, we route to reserved capacity or queue rather than swapping models. we should list fallback policy in the contract appendix.

elena: good notes. updated acceptance criteria (proposal):
- Functional: all acceptance tests pass for degraded flows (no crashes, proper 4xx on throttled requests)
- Latency targets: p95 <= 220ms for paid tier under nominal load; p95 <= 480ms for free tier. (degraded mode: p95 <= 700ms max)
- Error budget: define monthly error budget per tenant; automated soft-throttle starts when 30% of monthly budget burned in a 6h window; hard actions when 60% burned in 1h.
- Canary: 10% traffic for 24h with synthetic prompt set and user-simulated long prompts.
- Rollout gating: no >5% customer impact before SRE + ML signoff.

kevin: implementation sketch for throttler (gateway-level):
```
# pseudocode
if tenant.error_budget.burn_rate > soft_threshold:
  throttle(tenant, rate=0.8)  # reduce allowed QPS to 80%
if tenant.error_budget.burn_rate > hard_threshold:
  if tenant.fallback_policy.allows_auto_fallback:
    switch_model(tenant, model_variant="7b-quant")
  else:
    enqueue(tenant.requests, max_queue_ms=2000)
```
We can enforce per-tenant max_concurrency + a global shedder based on queue latency.

maya: edge cases to test (we should add these to PRD):
- cache stampede: many cold clients causing KV miss storms on startup. test with ramp of 1000 new sessions in 5m.
- long-tail prompts: single request with 20k tokens pushing mem/kv limits. ensure per-request token cap and graceful 4xx with clear retry guidance.
- region failover: if eu region capacity constrained, can we reroute to us with latency cap? include policy for geo-sensitive tenants.
- billing reconciliation when we throttle or downgrade model: customers should not be billed full rate when run on downgraded model.

jamal: add quality-gate snippet for fallback: when switching models automatically run quick eval of 50 golden prompts and check similarity metric > threshold. if fails, fallback abort and queue to reserved capacity. cheap to run (local inference on canary machines).

ops-bot: canary-run triggered by @elena. ID c-run-2212345678. start time 2026-03-18T09:12Z.

elena: next steps / owners:
- kevin: implement gateway throttle + queue prototype (owner)
- maya: define alert rules, run chaos tests for cache stampede (owner)
- jamal: create quality gate mini-eval and list of golden prompts (owner)
- sarah: draft contract clause for fallback policy and reserved-capacity billing adjustments (owner)

kevin: timeline: prototype in eng-sandbox by Mon, canary infra ready Wed. any blockers?

maya: blocker: need test harness for warm-cache simulation. i'll spin up a small job.

sarah: FYI i'll flag top 5 enterprise customers to legal for fallback-option consent.

elena: thanks all. I'll merge this addendum into the PRD and open an RFC thread for the implementation plan. please drop any final edge cases here before EOD. :pray:
